title: Incremental shard reconcile job for cost allocation and late-event handling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current daily ledger aggregation misses late-arriving metering events and suffers cross-region duplication when customers have multi-region deployments. This causes billing mismatches, manual adjustments, and delayed credits. Goal: Implement an incremental, sharded reconciliation job that consumes the canonical usage stream + raw audit logs to produce idempotent, tenant-scoped ledger deltas that resolve late events, dedupe cross-region duplicates, and generate backfill candidates for billing adjustments. The job must support dry-run validation, safety watermarking, and bounded reprocessing windows to keep compute cost predictable. Success criteria: 1) Reduce manual invoice adjustments by 90% for affected customers; 2) Reconcile >99.9% of late events within the configured reprocess window; 3) Produce deterministic, idempotent ledger writes and human-readable reconciliation reports for finance and support.
acceptance_criteria: Job can be executed in dry-run mode and produces reconciliation report without mutating ledger
Idempotent ledger delta writes with at-least-once semantics guarded by dedupe keys
Cross-region duplicates deduplicated using (request_id, model, tenant, truncated_timestamp) heuristic
System maintains per-shard watermark and exposes metrics for lag, processed-events, and reprocess-rate
Automated tests cover late event window boundaries and concurrent shard processing
Runbook updated and supportable by on-call with <60 minute run-to-stable target for common failure modes
implementation_notes: Architecture: new Reconciler lambda (k8s job) reads from canonical usage topic + raw audit S3 partition, groups by tenant-shard, computes delta using last_checkpoint, emits idempotent ledger patches to ledger-service v2 API
Shard key: tenant_id % N + daily_bucket to bound state size. N tuned to current tenant cardinality; initial N=128 for rollout
Watermarking: store per-shard processed_event_ts in distributed checkpoint store (DynamoDB with conditional writes) to avoid duplicate processing
Late-event logic: events up to 72 hours considered within default reprocess window; beyond that require manual approval flag
Dedupe heuristic: primary key (global_event_id) if present, fallback to (request_id, model_id, tenant_id, floor(ts/60s))
Backfill strategy: generate backfill jobs that annotate ledger delta with backfill_reason and backfill_window to allow finance to audit
Performance: use micro-batching and parallel shard workers; aim for 100k events/s cluster throughput during catch-up
Safety: dry-run first on staging with representative production replay; follow with opt-in canary to 1% of tenants then 10% before full rollout
rollout_plan: Staging: run full replay on last 7 days, validate reports with finance and support dashboards
Canary-1: run live dry-run for 1% tenant sample (non-billing) and compare with existing ledger aggregates
Canary-2: enable write-path for 1% tenants with auto-rollback on >0.5% divergence from expected deltas
Ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks with monitoring gates
Post-rollout: run a 7-day reconciliation sweep and produce variance report for finance
telemetry_and_checks: SLOs: reconciliation latency (event ingestion -> ledger delta) P95 < 15m within reprocess window
Dashboards: Console Analytics -> Reconciler L1 (lag, throughput, error rate) and Reconciliation Reports for finance
Alerting: pager if failed_writes_rate > 0.5% for 5m or if per-shard lag > reprocess_window
Queries: sample BigQuery SQL to validate totals vs ledger (linked in comment)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental double-charging due to race between reconciler and real-time billing pipeline. Mitigation: ledger-service v2 supports conditional apply_idempotency tokens and reconciliation run_id; reconciler writes include reconciliation_run_id and confirmation step in billing pipeline
Risk: checkpoint store hotspot on high-volume tenants. Mitigation: use adaptive shard splits and per-tenant rate limits; monitor DynamoDB throttles
Risk: resource cost during large backfills. Mitigation: throttled catch-up with priority lanes and finance approval for >7-day backfills
Risk: unseen dedupe edge cases for older events. Mitigation: keep original raw events in S3 archive for audit and provide finance-facing reconciliation CSVs
